outcome: admission to neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: 298 women who underwent a second stage cesarean section with a fetal head at or below the level of their ischial spines
finding: This study compared maternal and neonatal outcomes of the 'Push method' and 'Patwardhan's method' for fetal head delivery during a second-stage cesarean section, finding that while maternal complications were similar, neonatal complications were higher with 'Patwardhan's method'.
mod_finding: The use of 'Patwardhan's method' during a second-stage cesarean section was associated with higher rates of neonatal complications (neonatal sepsis and admission to NICU) compared to the 'Push method'.
